_info: This template documents the shape of project-level config files stored at {PROJECT_AGENTS}/project/.local-config.json (i.e. {USER_AGENTS}/{PROJECT_NAME}/project/.local-config.json). It is tracked in git so new installs know the expected structure. The live config files are NEVER in the repo — they live under the project-level framework directory.

_convention.rule: On local developer machines, all local-only configuration lives under the user-level framework directory (~/.agents/ on Unix, %USERPROFILE%\.agents\ on Windows). Global identity and preferences are root-level files; system-wide credentials unrelated to any project live at {USER_AGENTS}/project/. Project credentials and state live at {PROJECT_AGENTS}/project/.local-config.json, optionally segregated per environment under {PROJECT_AGENTS}/project/environments/. Credentials are never stored at repo level (sole exception: a plain identifier the user explicitly requested, after a second confirmation in chat). This file is the local-machine default only — sandboxed/hosted agents resolve credentials and state via the layered resolution chains in AGENTS.md (secret manager / env vars for credentials; {PROJECT_AGENTS} tiers for state) and never create this file on ephemeral or shared filesystems.

tier_structure.identity: {USER_AGENTS}/identity.json — author name and email, shared across all projects
tier_structure.preferences: {USER_AGENTS}/preferences.json — framework version, update check state, global defaults
tier_structure.framework_files: {USER_AGENTS}/directives/, standards/, skills/, workflows/, documentation/, project/ — installed from master repo, shared across all projects
tier_structure.common_templates: {USER_AGENTS}/common/templates/ — ticket template, board template, reusable scaffolding
tier_structure.project_config: {PROJECT_AGENTS}/project/.local-config.json — project-specific credentials (Jira, org aliases, etc.); per-environment overrides under {PROJECT_AGENTS}/project/environments/{env}/
tier_structure.project_tickets: {PROJECT_AGENTS}/project/tickets/ — local ticket files, shared by every repo/branch/worktree of the project; on local machines they persist across branches and sessions (in constrained environments, persistence is limited to what the resolved {PROJECT_AGENTS} tier provides)
tier_structure.project_board: {PROJECT_AGENTS}/project/board/ — agile board lanes (same persistence scope as tickets)
tier_structure.project_environment: {PROJECT_AGENTS}/project/ENVIRONMENT.md — this developer's env facts (org aliases, auth status); per developer, never shared or committed
tier_structure.project_workflows: {PROJECT_AGENTS}/workflows/ — project-specific workflows (incl. skill-helper orchestration); same-named file overrides the generic framework workflow for this project
tier_structure.project_directives: {PROJECT_AGENTS}/directives/ — project-specific directives; same-named file overrides the generic framework directive for this project
tier_structure.project_skills: {PROJECT_AGENTS}/skills/{skill-name}/{SKILL_NAME}_HELPER.md — bridges user-tier skills to this project's environments and credentials
tier_structure.temp: {OS temp}/.agents/{PROJECT_NAME}/ — transient data in the platform temp directory (%TEMP% on Windows, $TMPDIR//tmp on Unix); the OS owns cleanup

_convention.project_name_derivation: The {PROJECT_NAME} is the repository name from the git remote URL — e.g. https://github.com/rpoorun/rehlko-dtt.git gives 'rehlko-dtt'. If no git remote is configured, the agent asks for the project name in chat and persists it in the repo-level .agents/project/ configuration. Repos sharing the same remote name share one project tier.
_convention.how_to_add: 1. Add a new top-level key to this template with empty placeholder values. 2. Document the key in the skill's SKILL.md under 'Credential Loading' or 'Local Config'. 3. The install flow reads {PROJECT_AGENTS}/project/.local-config.json, detects blank fields under its key, and prompts the user only for what is missing. 4. Never create parallel local config files or directories.
_convention.naming: Use lowercase, short, descriptive key names (e.g. 'jira', 'slack', 'github'). Nest related fields one level deep. Do not nest deeper than two levels.
_convention.security: Keys that hold secrets (tokens, passwords, private keys) must be named clearly (e.g. 'api_token', 'secret'). The install flow must never echo secret values back to the user. The SKILL.md must document which fields are sensitive.
